verdict: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED — The Rp 8–18M/year range is plausible for combined T2DM + HTN + dyslipidaemia managed at private hospital rates with branded medications. However no single primary source states this combined private-rate figure. Evidence from peer-reviewed studies covers JKN (public insurance) rates which are materially lower (Rp 1.2M–3.6M/yr per condition). The private-rate estimate requires a bottom-up build from component cost data found in multiple primary sources.
primary_number: Rp 4.9M (~USD 308) per patient per year — IDF Atlas 11th edition (2024), Indonesia, population-average across all payer types. Private-rate per-condition estimates from peer-reviewed component data: DM outpatient direct cost Rp 1.8M–5.1M/yr (JKN); analogue insulin Rp 2.2M/yr (private pharmacy); SMBG strips Rp 1.6M/yr (private); specialist consults Rp 1.2M–16M/yr depending on tier. Bottom-up private-rate total for stable T2DM+HTN+dyslipidaemia: Rp 6M–20M/yr.
publisher: International Diabetes Federation (IDF) — Diabetes Atlas 11th Edition (2024)

cost_breakdown.consults: Private hospital specialist (internal medicine / endocrinologist): Rp 1,500,000–4,000,000 per visit (source: Alea.care 2025, insurance broker tariff guide); at 3–4 visits/year = Rp 4.5M–16M/year. Public hospital specialist: Rp 300,000–700,000 per visit (same source). JKN-rate COI study (Sultan Suriansyah, 2024, JIFI peer-reviewed): DM per-episode direct medical cost Rp 149,446; HTN per-episode Rp 98,264 — at 12 visits/year = Rp 1.8M (DM) and Rp 1.2M (HTN).
cost_breakdown.labs: HbA1c: approximately Rp 250,000–400,000/test at private labs; lipid panel: Rp 150,000–250,000/test; BUN/creatinine: Rp 100,000–150,000/test. Annual labs for stable T2DM (HbA1c 2x, lipid panel 2x, renal function 2x): Rp 1,000,000–1,600,000/year (bottom-up estimate from private lab pricing; not directly from a single primary source).
cost_breakdown.medication: Generic metformin + antihypertensive (amlodipine/ACEi) + statin: approximately Rp 50,000–150,000/month = Rp 600,000–1,800,000/year (JKN formulary prices). Branded equivalents: 3–5x higher. Analogue insulin (private pharmacy): USD 11.24/1000IU — source: Ramadaniati et al. 2024 (PLOS ONE, peer-reviewed). Peer-reviewed COI data: JKN outpatient chronic disease prescription = Rp 218,782/prescription (Rambe et al. 2025, Public Health of Indonesia); at 12 prescriptions/year = Rp 2.6M/year for medications alone under JKN rates.
cost_breakdown.devices: SMBG glucometer (private sector, online marketplace): median USD 18.37 = Rp 294,000 one-time (Ramadaniati et al. 2024, PLOS ONE). Test strips: USD 0.27/strip (online marketplace) to USD 0.36/strip (private pharmacy); at 1 test/day = USD 99–131/year = Rp 1.6M–2.1M/year. BP monitor: approximately Rp 200,000–600,000 one-time purchase. Annual device cost (stable T2DM with 1 SMBG/day): Rp 1.6M–2.1M.

methodology_note: No single peer-reviewed source provides a private-rate annual cost for combined T2DM+HTN+dyslipidaemia in Indonesia. Evidence triangulated from: (1) IDF Atlas 11th ed. national per-patient expenditure (all payers, USD 308.2/yr); (2) COI studies at public hospitals under JKN (Rp 149,446–208,652 per episode); (3) Peer-reviewed private sector device/insulin pricing (PLOS ONE 2024); (4) Peer-reviewed outpatient drug cost data (Public Health of Indonesia 2025); (5) Insurance tariff guides for private consultation fees. JKN studies systematically understate private OOP costs as they use insurance claim rates. Private-rate estimate of Rp 8–18M is consistent with bottom-up calculation but rests on combining multiple component sources, not one authoritative primary source for the aggregate figure.

recommended_edit_to_canonical: Revise the claim to distinguish JKN-insured versus private-rate OOP costs explicitly. Suggested revision: 'Annual out-of-pocket cost of managing stable T2DM+HTN+dyslipidaemia at private facilities in Indonesia is estimated at Rp 6M–20M per patient per year (approximately USD 375–1,250), depending on facility tier, medication choice (generic vs. branded), and SMBG frequency. By comparison, IDF Atlas 11th edition (2024) estimates Indonesia's all-payer average diabetes health expenditure at USD 308/person/year, and JKN-rate peer-reviewed studies (Sultan Suriansyah hospital, Banjarmasin, 2024) report per-episode direct medical costs of Rp 149,000–209,000 for DM and Rp 98,000–168,000 for HTN, consistent with Rp 1.8M–2.5M/year under the public insurance system. The Rp 8–18M/year figure applies to private-rate patients combining consultant fees (Rp 1.5M–4M/visit x 3–4 visits), branded medications (~Rp 1.8M–5M/year), routine labs (~Rp 1M–1.6M/year), and SMBG devices (~Rp 1.6M–2.1M/year). Sources: IDF Atlas 11th ed. (diabetesatlas.org, 2024); Ramadaniati et al. PLOS ONE 2024 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0309350); Rambe et al. Public Health of Indonesia 2025 (doi:10.36685/phi.v11i3.1036); JIFI COI study Sultan Suriansyah 2024 (e-jurnal.stikes-isfi.ac.id).'
